description.narrative: Syftet med bidraget är att arbeta under en ekosystemansats som syftar till att upprätthålla ett komplex av sammankopplade biomer av skog-gräsmark-våtmarker, Chaco och Pantanal. De föreslår att arbeta i enlighet med cykeln: bevarande - hållbar ekonomisk produktion - social påverkan - bevarande, som involverar olika offentliga, privata och civila samhällets aktörer med viktiga roller i territoriet.

The aim of the contribution is to work under an ecosystem approach that seeks to maintain a complex of interconnected biomes of forest-grassland-wetlands, of the Chaco and Pantanal. They propose to work complying with the cycle: conservation - sustainable economic production - social impact - conservation, involving different public, private and civil society actors with important roles in the territory.

The current intervention aims to contribute to the conservation of the Great Landscape in Bolivia. This will be done by i) strengthening institutional capacities for the comprehensive management of natural risks and the effects of climate change, ii) favouring sustainable living systems towards a comprehensive economy that promotes the generation and commercialization of products free of deforestation, iii) promoting the active participation of vulnerable groups such as women, indigenous people and peasant communities.
To achieve this task, four specific objectives have been established:
- To strengthen institutional and organizational capacities for the conservation of the Great Landscape, through the management of natural and anthropogenic risks and the effects of climate change with emphasis on the comprehensive management of fire as the main threat, heritage management natural resources, connectivity and water security
- To promote the implementation and development of sustainable production chains that improve and ensure the livelihoods of local populations, communities and indigenous peoples through good practices, innovations and added value; promoting the production, promotion and marketing of deforestation-free products compatible with conservation and adaptation to climate change.
- To generate processes of consultation, training, research, permanent technical and technological innovation, promoting the participation of women, indigenous peoples and peasants in decision-making that contribute to good environmental governance and territorial management.
- To strengthen multi-stakeholder networks in the Chaco - Pantanal region, as coordination bodies at the national and international level, enhancing the impact of actions in the territory, on topics such as: the conservation of natural heritage, sustainable production and resilience to climate change.
At the end of the intervention, it is expected that:
-9M Ha will be in better conditions of protection, connectivity and conservation; with local/departmental governments and protected area managers strengthened and effectively managing their territories to reduce risks from forest fires implementing policies and strategies for adaptation to climate change, generating conditions of resilience at the local level and enhancing access to climate financing.
- At least 100,000 Ha will be under good productive practices with a focus on environmental sustainability that prevent deforestation and forest degradation, and contribute to the valuation of natural heritage and its environmental functions, with better conditions of food security, family economy and climate resilience.
- At least 1000 Women, youth, technicians, indigenous peoples and farmers of the Chaco - Pantanal landscape are empowered and have better technical and technological training
- At least 3 regional collaborative alliances that promote a joint agenda that guides interventions in the territory with a focus on conservation, sustainability and climate resilience have been strengthened.

description.narrative:
During this second period of implementation, 9 million hectares benefited from integrated fire management and strengthened protection. Technical and operational capacities were enhanced, through coordination among municipalities, Indigenous autonomies, and national protected areas. Progress in passive restoration of 1.2 million hectares in the ACIE Ñembi Guasu, ensuring that under the leadership of GAIOC Charagua, an ecological pause is maintained in the territory.
Regarding Fire Management, Nativa has supported the implementation of the Strategic Plan for Integrated Fire Management in 6 municipalities, including regional training, coordination and support in emergency response (strengthening of local capacities). 8 community-based first response brigades against forest fires in the Greater ChacoPantanal Landscape, distributed across 6 communities in the municipality of Roboré, 2 in Carmen Rivero Torrez, and 2 in Puerto Suárez have been strengthened.
Regarding the results oriented to promote sustainable production models, Implementation of a forest-based livestock model that includes farm-level planning, sustainable forage management, efficient water management, strengthening of associative spaces, and biodiversity monitoring across 55,000 hectares, benefiting more than 60 producers and 19 associations in the Chaco Tarijeño region is implemented.
Nativa has also supported 312 beekeepers (organized into 12 associations) through technical assistance, continuous training, and support in product traceability. This has improved the quality and sustainability of Chaco honey, recognized internationally for its value, and facilitated access to fair trade channels, promoting the product as an organic good from a highly ecologically fragile territory. In the artisanal sector, work is being done with 200 artisan producers, including Indigenous Guaraní, Weenhayek, and Chiquitano men and women, strengthening their capacities to develop sustainable and traceable productsfrom the natural origin of their inputs to their commercializationthrough the Alma de Monte commercial strategy. Also during this period, the Alma de Monte brand with 7 points of sale across 3 departments has been consolidated, covering more than 200 producers and artisans; and partnerships with various productive organizations.
The project TEKOVE has also supported the strengthening of local and territorial organizations through the promotion of Free, Prior, and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes for the participatory development and validation of Climate Action Plans (PACC), ensuring the effective involvement of Indigenous and peasant communities in each allied autonomous territorial entity.
In Bajo Isoso, work was carried out with the Guaraní people to consolidate the Yandé Yari protected area, based on Indigenous worldview and the need to protect the Bañados del Isoso, a key wetland for water regulation and food security in the territory. Within the Pilcomayo Corridor framework, actions were coordinated with Indigenous peoples, local organizations, and authorities to jointly build a proposal for the comprehensive conservation of the lower basin, safeguarding the only surface watercourse in the Chaco against threats such as deforestation and forest fragmentation.
Key technical and legal support was provided in the Preventive Action in Defense of Ñembi Guasu process, aiming to declare the ACIE Ñembi Guasu as untouchable public land, ensuring its integrity as a conservation area and preventing deforestation authorizations by the ABT and land allocations by the INRA. This legal action, currently under review by the Plurinational Agro-Environmental Court, represents a historic precedent in the defense of Indigenous territories and environmental conservation in Bolivia.
Technical and legal advice was provided to prevent the construction of a high-impact binational road that would threaten the conservation of the ACIE Ñembi Guasu and, consequently, the ecological connectivity of the KaaiyaÑembi GuasuOtuquis corridor. Thanks to this support, the GAIOC has submitted formal objections, with explicit backing from Indigenous organizations, reflecting a unified stance in defense of biocultural heritage. This process strengthens Indigenous territorial governance and highlights a replicable high-value conservation model.
Regarding the development of environmental policies at national and subnational levels, Nativa has supported the validation of the Departmental Climate Change Policy of Tarija, a key instrument that integrates the climate approach into public policies, territorial planning, and resilient development. Together with GAIOC Charagua Iyambae, legislative processes were promoted, resulting in the approval of the Protected Areas Law of the Indigenous Autonomy and specific regulations for the management of the Ñembi Guasu Area of Conservation and Ecological Importance (ACIE). Additionally, official approval of the Climate Action Plan of Puerto Suárez, establishing a legal framework that enables the management of funds and strategic projects related to climate adaptation and mitigation has been accomplished.
Finaly, in the women economic empowerment, 400 women from Indigenous communities in the Greater ChacoPantanal Landscape have strengthen their capacities in sustainable value chains related to beekeeping and artisanal production, contributing to both the local economy and ecosystem conservation.
